core_dynamic: Leadership, independence, drive + Leadership, independence, drive
what_works_well: Together they combine decisive, action-oriented, initiates with decisive, action-oriented, initiates, creating potential for complementary strengths when roles are clear and respected.
where_it_breaks: When under pressure, 1 tends to lean into its dominant traits while 1 reacts from its own pattern. This often creates misalignment in expectations, communication gaps, and frustration over pace or priorities. Without awareness, both individuals may feel misunderstood and begin working against each other instead of as a team.
best_roles: 1 leads through its natural strengths while 1 supports in areas that complement rather than compete.
conflict_solution: The key is to define expectations early and revisit them regularly. Both sides must understand not just their own tendencies but how they impact the other person in practice. Clear communication, defined roles, and structured feedback loops prevent recurring conflict patterns.
guidance: This only works if you divide power immediately. If both of you try to lead everything, you'll burn the partnership down fast. Respect is shown through staying in your lane, not competing. Schedule alignment meetings or this turns into constant silent rivalry.
warning: You will slowly stop collaborating and start competing. Small decisions will turn into battles, communication will break down, and eventually one of you will disengage or force a split.
